- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or weak; adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% for first 5–7 days if sentiment <0.33.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model lags in correction; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply gradual downward slope.
- If model forecast is >75.00 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For sentiment history with alternating +/– signals, model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-based adjustment.
